extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans, benchmarking 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples. It addresses two primary issues in existing benchmarks: visual content being unnecessary for many samples, and unintentional data leakage in LLM and LVLM training.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao (University of Science and Technology of China, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shanghai AI Laboratory)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks (SEED, AI2D, ScienceQA, MMBench, MathVista, MMMU) with an automated pipeline using LLM inspectors, then manually reviewed by three experts to ensure visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and advanced multi-modal capability requirements.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples collected from six existing multi-modal benchmarks: MMMU (MMMU-Val), MMBench (MMBench-EN-Dev), ScienceQA (ScienceQA-Test), AI2D (AI2D-Test), SEED (SEED-Image), and MathVista (MathVista-Mini).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated pipeline was used to filter out samples answerable by more than 2 of 8 LLM inspectors. Samples were split into four difficulty categories (easy, moderate, hard, tough) based on hit counts from 16 LVLMs. The sample pool was reduced from 22,401 to 11,607 after coarse filtering, and then to 1,500 after manual review.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted manual review to ensure: 1) each sample's answer should be based on the understanding of visual content; 2) selected samples should cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; 3) most samples should require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution. Samples were also split into four difficulty categories based on LVLM hit counts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Samples were split into four difficulty levels (easy: 12-16 LVLM hits, moderate: 8-11, hard: 4-7, tough: 0-3) based on hit counts from 16 LVLMs on the coarsely filtered samples, to guide manual selection with diversity in difficulty.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Eight LLMs used as automated inspectors: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B; 16 LVLMs used to gauge difficulty; VLMEvalKit used as evaluation codebase.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark sources are skewed toward SEED (28.3% of final 1,500 samples), MMBench (24.4%), and MathVista (23.0%), with less representation from ScienceQA (4.6%) and MMMU (6.7%) after manual review.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Even the best model scores under 60% on average on MMStar. The benchmark currently consists of only 1,500 samples. Data leakage and visual dependency issues may still exist in other benchmarks not addressed by MMStar.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of large vision-language models (LVLMs) on multi-modal capabilities across 6 core dimensions and 18 detailed axes. Also used to measure data leakage (ML) and actual multi-modal performance gain (MG) in multi-modal training.
